audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL components (EVM memory, transaction validation, precompiles, hexadecimal parsing, EIP-1559 fee market) and CL-adjacent components (validator consolidation via EIP-7251, beacon chain interactions in Paris). Also includes wallet permission model (EIP-2255) which spans the dApp-wallet boundary.

out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals beyond Engine API interface

misclassified_entities.reason: A calling contract within the EVM is an internal component of the Execution Layer, not an external entity. It executes within the same trust boundary as the EVM itself.

When appearing in EIP-7251 effective balance subgraph, the Beacon Chain is the CL itself — an in-scope target component, not an external entity. It should be modeled as the CL component interacting with the EL via Engine API.
Duplicate of EXT-DAPP — same external entity (dApp) calling restricted wallet methods. Consolidated into EXT-DAPP-JSON-RPC.
Duplicate of EXT-DAPP — same external entity querying permissions. Consolidated into EXT-DAPP-JSON-RPC.
Duplicate of EXT-DAPP — a malicious dApp is the same entity type with adversarial intent. Consolidated into EXT-DAPP-JSON-RPC with UNTRUSTED trust level.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users and dApps submit transactions via the public JSON-RPC API. No authentication required. All transaction data (type, fees, blob data, init code) must be fully validated. Covers EXT-TX-SUBMITTER, EXT-TX-SENDER, EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator operators submit consolidation and exit requests as regular EVM transactions to the predeploy contract. No special authentication — anyone can call the contract. Fee and format validation is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with the EL via the Engine API, authenticated with JWT. The channel is authenticated but payload content (block headers, execution payloads) must still be validated: sequential block numbers, zero difficulty/nonce, empty ommers, correct state/transaction/receipt roots, base fee correctness.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Validator via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators propose blocks and submit attestations over P2P. Any validator may be malicious. Proposed blocks must be fully validated (PoS rules: zero difficulty, zero nonce, empty ommers hash). Attestations must be verified against the validator registry.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Hex Input Source via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC parameters (gas values, block numbers, addresses as hex strings)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Hex-encoded data enters the EL via JSON-RPC parameters. No authentication. Input may contain invalid hex characters, overlong strings, or values exceeding type bounds (U8, U64, U256). All parsing must validate format and enforce type constraints.

trusted_external_entities.name: dApp via Wallet JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: dApps interact with wallets via JSON-RPC. No inherent trust — any dApp may be malicious. Permission requests may contain crafted URLs (SSRF), over-broad capability requests, or spoofed invoker identities. All permission checks and caveat validations must be enforced.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: peer nodes propagate blocks and transactions over devp2p. Any peer may be malicious. Eclipse attacks, invalid block injection, and transaction spam are all possible. All received data must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV-Boost Relay / External Service
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: MEV-Boost relay API, checkpoint sync endpoints
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: external services like MEV relays and checkpoint sync providers can supply incorrect data, censor transactions, or denial-of-service validators. No inherent trust should be placed in their responses.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full validation required: request format (20+48+48 bytes), fee computation via exponential formula, fee sufficiency check, queue capacity check (262,144 limit). Insufficient fee results in rejection; queue overflow silently discards without refund.
Exit weight must be computed and checked against epoch churn limit (256 ETH). Excess exits are deferred. Weight-based churn limiting prevents rapid validator set changes.

Full transaction validation required: type decoding (EIP-2718), fee cap constraints (max_fee >= priority_fee, max_fee >= base_fee), blob-specific validation (gas limit, blob fee, versioned hash, data presence), init code size limits, nonce matching, balance sufficiency, sender EOA check, signature recovery.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API newPayload / Block State Transition
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Content validation required despite JWT authentication: sequential block number, increasing timestamp, gas limit bounds, zero difficulty, zero nonce, empty ommers hash (keccak256 of RLP([])), state root verification, transaction root verification, receipt root verification, logs bloom verification, base fee correctness per EIP-1559 formula.

Full PoS consensus validation: difficulty == 0, nonce == 0, ommers hash == EMPTY_OMMER_HASH, valid proposer signature, valid attestations. Malicious validators may propose invalid blocks or conflicting attestations.

Input validation required: valid hex characters only (0-9, a-f, A-F), optional 0x prefix handling, fixed-size output enforcement via padding, type bounds checking by U8/U64/U256/Uint wrappers. Invalid input must raise errors, not silently produce incorrect values.

Full permission validation required: invoker identity verification (no spoofing), user consent prompt (no clickjacking), caveat enforcement on restricted methods, URL validation against SSRF (scheme and port whitelisting), permission isolation per invoker origin. Permissions must be filtered by invoker for getPermissions.

All blocks and transactions received from P2P must undergo the same full validation as locally submitted data. No trust should be placed in peer-provided data. Rate limiting and resource bounds must be enforced to prevent DoS.

Relay-provided execution payloads must be fully validated before inclusion. Checkpoint sync data must be verified against known state roots. No trust should be placed in relay availability or data integrity without independent verification.
